//: Type-checks the page's own JavaScript without changing a byte of it.
allowJs + checkJs is the whole point: the assets stay plain classic
scripts that the browser loads directly, and this reads them where they
sit. There is no emit, no bundle and no output directory, so nothing
here can end up in the binary.
moduleDetection is left at its default deliberately. The assets share one
global scope by design, because the CSP allows no inline script and a
module import could not carry the token. A file with no import or export
is a script to the checker too, which is what lets app.js see el() from
ui.js instead of reporting every helper as undefined.
strict is off. These are DOM builders written against a browser, not a
typed codebase, and turning it on would mean annotating every closure to
buy warnings about nulls that the page already handles. What is on is the
part that pays: undefined names, misspelled properties, wrong argument
counts and calls into things that are not functions.
